      "content": "# Aviary in Applications\n\nApplications opens the original Aviary migration workspace with its existing Python executable. The same source, SQLite database, mapping revisions, native packages, API operation IDs, upload progress and complete handoffs remain available in the original browser and CLI.\n\n## Prepare the collection once\n\nUse the original source directory and mapping described in [the operator guide](README.md):\n\n~~~sh\nstarforge aviary --python /absolute/python3 init \\\n  --source /private/original-collection \\\n  --workspace /private/aviary-workspace \\\n  --mapping /private/reviewed-mapping.json\n~~~\n\nFor a complete handoff, the original receiver opens its retained application and workspace:\n\n~~~sh\nstarforge aviary --python /absolute/python3 receive \\\n  --source /private/Aviary_Complete_Workspace.zip \\\n  --output /private/aviary-received\n~~~\n\nSelect /private/aviary-received/workspace in Applications after receiving. The native receiver preserves the workspace ID, original files, saved mapping history, API operation records and provider IDs from that handoff.\n\nThe installed aviary command exposes the complete original init, show, preview, mapping, save-mapping, assign-keys, package, export, plan, run, reconcile, refresh-upload, transcripts and receive commands. The same entry can run directly as node research/aviary/cli.mjs, with the surrounding source path appropriate to the selected package.\n\n## Review and open\n\n1. Open the maintained runtime workspace and choose a READY runtime containing the research-aviary contribution.\n2. Choose Applications, then **Aviary collection migration**.\n3. Select the saved workspace directory and the existing Python 3.11 or later executable. This application uses Python's standard library.\n4. Choose a local port, or use zero to let the original server choose a free port. Select the existing private environment file when the original API operation needs its named credential variable.\n5. Review the application, save it, review Start and start it. Open follows the actual listener reported by the original Python server.\n\nReview reads the native workspace identity, original source-manifest identity and selected Python. It retains the complete native application source and the selected runtime. Start checks that same binding before the original server opens. The live launch endpoint must agree with the announced workspace, source, Python and process before Applications exposes Open.\n\nA source collection can contain large media. Application review reads the retained source manifest and native identity without rescanning every media byte. The original native preview, package, upload and export methods retain their existing source verification.\n\n## Operate the collection\n\nUse the original five-table browser to inspect resources, media, transcripts, indexes and supplements. Save explicit mapping revisions, retain native user keys, review exclusions and visibility, and produce the complete native import ZIP. The original source remains available alongside the mapped rows.\n\nAPI planning and execution use the collection's existing configuration and original operation ID. Enter the actual organization, collection and token environment name through the native workflow. Those settings and the entered receiver's responses stay in the original migration records.\n\nIf an upload or resource action needs recovery, open the same saved operation. The original client retains remote resource/media IDs and accepted upload parts. Reconcile a lost creation reply with that original action, or refresh an upload manifest for the same original media/upload ID. The original API client's cooldown and source checks remain in effect.\n\n## Stop and reopen\n\nStop controls the existing managed command and its original Python process. Mapping revisions, local source, accepted operations, native child actions and completed files stay in the saved workspace. Reopen the same saved application and use Review Start to open that workspace again.\n\nThe workbench marks a prior unfinished operator job as interrupted. Open its original API operation to continue from the recorded action and upload state. A changed native runtime or replaced workspace identity requires the existing review flow to select that change explicitly.\n\nApplications retains the actual effective port, including canonical HTTP port 80 and a server-assigned port. Reopening on another free port preserves the workspace ID and saved collection state.\n\n## Complete receiving\n\nExport from the original browser or CLI:\n\n~~~sh\nstarforge aviary --python /absolute/python3 export \\\n  --workspace /private/aviary-workspace \\\n  --output /private/delivery/Aviary_Complete_Workspace.zip\n~~~\n\nThe original handoff contains the native application, original collection, source manifest, every saved mapping revision, API plan/action journal, retained provider IDs, transcript downloads and human review. It now also carries managed.py and this guide, so the original application's binding and launch commands remain available in the received native source.\n\nReceive the complete ZIP through the original receive command, then choose its workspace directory in a READY runtime containing this contribution. Review selects that runtime's native source and Python while retaining the received workspace and migration records. Completed remote actions retain their original provider IDs and original source relationships.\n\n## Source entry points\n\n| Entry | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| aviary.py | Original native collection, package, API and receiving commands |\n| cli.mjs | Installed Node command forwarding to the selected Python |\n| managed.py | Original workspace/source/Python binding and managed native launch |\n| application.mjs | Applications preparation and live startup reader |\n| application-provider.mjs | Source-owned catalog and lifecycle registration |\n| server.py | Original browser operator and live listener identity |\n| distribution/contributions/research-aviary.json | Complete installed source and command declaration |\n\nThe application kind and installed managed command are aviary-workspace; the provider is research-aviary. Existing saved workspaces keep their original native IDs. The source owner retains the original collection intake and complete API/browser receiving operation.\n"

      "content": "# Aviary: complete browser receiving and interruption recovery\n\nThis companion runs the original public-source operator journey against the\nmaintained Aviary application. It opens the already completed native migration\nas the saved-operation example. It does not create a second provider migration.\n\nThe earlier browser runner did not reach its first UI action: publisher-page\nintake stopped before the public workspace and browser were started. This v2\nrunner therefore establishes its receiving identity before the first actual\nbrowser mutation. The application and its ten maintained runtime files remain\nunchanged.\n\n## Source and entry points\n\nThe existing repository entry is:\n\n    stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/research/aviary/examples/run-aviary-browser-receiving.mjs\n\nPlace its Python companion in the same directory:\n\n    examples/aviary_browser_support.py\n\nThis guide is:\n\n    examples/AVIARY_BROWSER_RECEIVING.md\n\nThe current application source is the complete Aviary closure from PR2164,\nhead a33feb2ecbd952e2a46245b7f367a86eac787b54 before this receiving-only successor.\nThe runtime files are aviary.py, aviary_client.py, server.py, index.html, app.js,\ncli.mjs, README.md, PROVIDER_CONTRACT.md, managed.py and APPLICATIONS.md. The\nrunner verifies the five reviewed core/client/server/UI Git blob identities and\nrecords the exact SHA-256 and length of all ten files. A repeated invocation\nmust use the same complete source and the same original input directories.\n\nThis is a receiving companion. It is not an additional application server or a\nprovider client implementation. The Python bridge imports the actual selected\naviary.py and calls its original mapping, preview, serialization, ZIP\nverification, packaging and export functions.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\nUse the completed original native receiving workspace and its existing\noperation ID. Every action in that selected operation must already have the\nmaintained successful state CONFIRMED or ADOPTED. The browser reads those\noriginal provider IDs and retains them unchanged.\n\nThe public workspace must contain the completed original USGS source example:\ntwo resource rows, three media rows, one transcript row, two index rows and two\nsupplemental rows. Complete the original publisher/rights/transcript intake\nbefore starting this journey. Reuse the five previously captured public\nbinaries; the browser companion does not fetch them again.\n\nThe two workspaces must be distinct. The application directory must contain\naviary.py directly. Use Python 3.11 or newer and an existing Node/Playwright/\nChromium installation.\n\nThe existing verified host has:\n\n    Node:\n    /opt/codex/runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin/node\n\n    Playwright 1.62.1:\n    /opt/codex/runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs\n\n    Chromium:\n    /workspace/scratch/705ebf077387/browser-runtime/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell\n\nThose paths describe the verified original host. A different receiving host\nmust supply its actual installed paths. The script neither installs packages\nnor downloads a browser.\n\n## Run the original journey\n\nUse the same command on a later invocation if the producing process is\ninterrupted. Keep the application, public workspace, original provider\nworkspace, operation ID and output directory unchanged.\n\n    node examples/run-aviary-browser-receiving.mjs \\\n      --application /absolute/path/to/aviary \\\n      --workspace /absolute/path/to/original-public-workspace \\\n      --provider-workspace /absolute/path/to/completed-native-workspace \\\n      --operation-id ORIGINAL_COMPLETED_NATIVE_OPERATION \\\n      --out /absolute/path/to/browser-receiving \\\n      --python python3 \\\n      --playwright-module /opt/codex/runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs \\\n      --browser-executable /workspace/scratch/705ebf077387/browser-runtime/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell\n\nEvery option is supplied at most once. The receiving output contains a stable\nidentity, original snapshots, original UI requests, response captures,\nhistorical commit evidence, original queued job IDs, the actual browser\ndownloads, capture descriptors and per-invocation process/drain records.\n\nThe root process that owns a private producing filesystem must retain that\nnamespace until the requested complete archives and reports have been saved.\nDo not assume an interactive PTY or private /dev directory will survive a\ndisconnected executor. Save the completed outputs through the already\nmaintained artifact helper before that producing context exits.\n\n## The complete operator path\n\n1. Open the original public workspace and inspect the complete source\n   inventory. Read the selected completed native operation before making any\n   public-workspace change.\n\n2. Assign Aviary resource and media keys through the original UI once. Record\n   the original expected revision and full saved document. The original key\n   allocator considers all source rows, including excluded rows, applies the\n   maintained defaults/column/value mappings, and allocates the first unused\n   four-digit keys. It also appends its review note; a repeated call would\n   create another review.\n\n3. Save a source-review note while delaying the actual response from the\n   original server. Type a later note before releasing that response. Confirm\n   the later input remains visible, remains unsaved and can be saved through\n   the ordinary UI. The request, response and typing observation are retained.\n\n4. Exclude one original resource using the actual reason dialog, save that\n   review, and then restore the same source row. Check all five source tables\n   through their normal preview controls. The final selection restores every\n   original example row.\n\n5. Queue the native CSV/assets package through the ordinary Delivery panel.\n   Retain the original job and its timestamped output path, then download that\n   exact completed archive through the browser.\n\n6. Queue and download the complete original application/workspace export.\n   Check its manifest, original review, source fingerprint and all ten\n   application members.\n\n7. Capture the public workspace at desktop and narrow widths, close the\n   original server, receive the first complete export through the maintained\n   CLI, and reopen that received application/workspace in the browser. Verify\n   its original identity, source bytes and saved mapping.\n\n8. Open the already completed native provider workspace, select the original\n   operation, enter a new destination draft, return to the saved operation and\n   then return to the new draft. Verify the entered draft is preserved and\n   select the original operation again. The Run, Reconcile and Prepare\n   controls are not invoked. Every original provider action and identifier\n   must remain unchanged.\n\n9. Capture that saved operation at desktop and narrow widths, close every\n   owned page, server, browser context, browser and CLI child, and only then\n   publish the final PASS result.\n\nThe browser's request guard allows the normal read/preview operations and the\nspecific recorded review/package/export requests. An unexpected provider,\nplanning, migration or reconciliation request aborts the journey.\n\n## Recovery uses the original committed evidence\n\n### Mapping and key allocation\n\nA request file is published before its original UI request is forwarded. On a\nlater invocation, the Python bridge reads the actual retained review revision\nthrough mapping(db, revision) and compares the document using the application's\nown digest function. That digest includes the original canonical JSON and\nterminal LF.\n\nIf the server committed the review but the response or phase receipt was lost,\nthe existing committed revision supplies the result. The request is not sent\nagain. If no commit exists, the original expected revision and before document\nmust still be current before the same request may proceed.\n\nThe assigned-key postimage is derived with the original mapped_tables,\neffective_values and KEY semantics, including excluded rows and the exact\nappended note. Calling allocate_keys to discover whether it previously\ncommitted would itself change the review, so recovery does not do that.\n\nA new unrelated current review is preserved. The runner stops before a pending\nmutation whose original expected revision no longer describes the current\nsaved review.\n\n### Delayed response and later typing\n\nThe held route has explicit completion/rejection promises, bounded fetch and\nrelease deadlines, and unconditional release and unroute cleanup. A failed\nfetch cannot leave the receiving process waiting on an unresolved promise.\n\nThe first committed note is retained even if the process stops before its\ntyping observation is published. The later note is completed through its\noriginal saved request. If the observation itself is absent, the runner\nrecords a separately numbered observation pair: save an explicitly labeled\ntemporary note with the real delayed response, then restore the exact final\nreview note. An interrupted pair is restored before a new numbered pair is\nstarted. No committed POST is replayed and no missing observation is claimed\nas measured.\n\n### Queued archives\n\nEach queue request retains the original pre-request job IDs, request body and\nselected source/review. The accepted job ID is retained from its actual HTTP\nresponse or uniquely reconciled from the original persisted job journal. An\nambiguous result is preserved for reconciliation rather than guessed.\n\nA restart of the maintained server marks old QUEUED/RUNNING jobs INTERRUPTED.\nIf the original ZIP exists, the bridge validates and reuses that exact file,\neven if the terminal response or sidecar publication was interrupted.\n\nFor a native ZIP whose sidecar was not published, the bridge reconstructs the\nexpected member descriptors from the original package_rows result, original\nfield order, CRLF CSV writer and retained assets, then calls the maintained\nverify_zip. It records a separate verification receipt; it does not invent or\nreplace an original sidecar.\n\nIf an original INTERRUPTED job has no final ZIP, the bridge first requires the\noriginal application server to have drained. It then invokes the same original\nbuild_package or export_workspace function with the exact already-published\noutput path and original selection. It preserves operator-jobs.json and saves\na separate completion receipt. It does not create another queued job or a new\ntimestamped output. A failed, conflicting, corrupt or ambiguously owned output\nis retained and reported.\n\n### Downloads and PNG capture\n\nThe browser download must match the original queued archive's exact length and\nSHA-256. Existing downloaded bytes are checked and reused. A missing download\nreceipt can be reconstructed from that same original queued file.\n\nA PNG capture records its exact pixel-file descriptor and observed viewport\nmetrics before publishing the final filename. If the process stops in that\ngap, the next invocation publishes the original captured bytes; it does not\nredraw different pixels over the first capture. The PNG type is explicit, even\nwhen a temporary filename ends with a receiving suffix.\n\n### Cold receiving and final drain\n\nThe first complete export remains the source of the original received\nworkspace. The maintained receive function can reopen that same archive while\npreserving its already received state. The runner never creates a replacement\nexport merely to obtain a new receiving path.\n\nThe output has one held kernel lock for the receiving owner. Native children\ncarry an operation/output-specific marker; an interrupted continuation checks\nand drains only its own retained process family. CLI results use closed\nstdout/stderr descriptors and bounded child termination.\n\nA completed application/drain candidate is retained before the final control\nlock is released. If publication of the final result is interrupted, the next\ninvocation verifies that candidate and its files, confirms the original\nprocesses are inactive and publishes the same result. It does not start a new\nbrowser journey in that final gap.\n\n## Outputs and their meaning\n\nThe final machine-readable result is:\n\n    browser-receiving-result.json\n\nIts schema is commons.aviary.complete-browser-receiving.v2. PASS means the\ncomplete browser/data-flow assertions succeeded and all owned application\nprocesses, browser resources and control children were drained before final\npublication. A failed invocation retains its own runs/<id>/failure.json and\nall earlier completed requests/outputs. It never replaces a completed PASS.\n\nThe two primary browser-downloaded artifacts are:\n\n    USGS_Aviary_Native_Package.zip\n    USGS_Aviary_Complete_Workspace.zip\n\nThe complete export contains the actual application, original workspace,\nsource, saved review, native package and handoff manifests. The received copy\nis retained under received-public.\n\nFour PNGs remain in the producing workspace for actual local visual review:\n\n    aviary-public-desktop.png\n    aviary-public-mobile.png\n    aviary-original-migration-desktop.png\n    aviary-original-migration-mobile.png\n\nTheir hashes and viewport checks are retained in the result. Independent image\ninspection remains explicitly PENDING until the actual PNGs are opened and\nreviewed. DOM checks alone do not claim visual acceptance. The actual producing owner will retain\nthe resulting native receipt, reviewed images and saved artifact identities\nfrom the single original continuation.\n"

      "content": "# Aviary provider contract\n\nThis application preserves an original catalogue, its reviewed Aviary mapping, the complete native import package, and each REST operation through receiving and recovery. [README.md](README.md) describes the operator workflow. This document records the provider interfaces and the evidence used to advance a saved migration.\n\n## Authoritative sources\n\n| Source | Retained identity and use |\n| --- | --- |\n| [Published OpenAPI schema](https://www.aviaryplatform.com/aviary-api.json) | HTTP 200 retrieved October 12, 2026 at 09:20:11 UTC; 200,348 bytes; SHA256 `1bf29e93ede6bc7aa755be25603e1fed4ddb899dac1964f4f63eaaca930c1291`; OpenAPI 3.0.0, API info version 1.0.0. The actual [documentation page](https://www.aviaryplatform.com/api/v1/documentation) names this schema. |\n| [AVP import/export repository](https://github.com/WeAreAVP/aviary-api-scripts/tree/9f189144f6434e6561696983edce17494aa66dd0) | Commit `9f189144f6434e6561696983edce17494aa66dd0`, dated September 29, 2026. Establishes the maintained JSON/form request conventions and native CSV fields. |\n| Full-package importer | Original Git blob `e8c612495fb851b1e756a32143c032feaa5d264d`; original media, metadata and thumbnail-URL parameter handling. |\n| Media importer | Original Git blob `20809b4ebd4024586a47e1a470d595d83fa48916`; presigned PUT, multipart identity and the original completion request. |\n| Transcript exporter | Original Git blob `0b57ecff919740a17fbdf71ac304f981221ebc7b`; resource transcript IDs, export format map and exact file receiving. |\n| [Native bulk-import guide](https://coda.aviaryplatform.com/bulk-importing-248) | Resource, media, transcript, index and supplemental CSV structure. |\n| [Aviary API guide](https://coda.aviaryplatform.com/aviary-api-14) | Organization API access and the published documentation route. |\n\nThe application is original implementation. The provider sources establish its interfaces. AVP's example Steve Zahn OHMS transcript has an explicit distribution restriction and is excluded from the source example. The public USGS example retains its own publisher and rights records.\n\nThe captured OpenAPI contains some malformed JSON examples and inconsistent example labels. These are retained as source limitations. Runtime responses must be valid JSON with the expected endpoint-specific identity; the client does not repair a response into a success.\n\n## Native package and mapping\n\nThe ZIP has one `aviary-package/` root. Its five CSV basenames match the provider's native templates. Every CSV uses UTF-8, explicit column order, proper quoting and complete row widths. Selected file paths refer to `/aviary-package/{asset-directory}/{filename}` within that archive. Filenames include a source-hash prefix. Equal source bytes are reused at one destination; a destination collision cannot substitute different bytes.\n\nResource User Key and Media User Key are separate four-digit namespaces, 1000–9999. They link original CSV rows within an import. Aviary does not preserve them as remote record lookup keys. The application retains the original catalogue identifiers and the reviewed key map, then records each actual provider ID separately.\n\nA local resource/media key and an existing Aviary parent ID are mutually exclusive selections. For media, an existing `aviary ID` identifies the resource. For transcripts and indexes it identifies the media file. For supplemental rows it identifies the resource. A local relationship resolves through the saved key map and the original parent's retained creation action.\n\nExplicit row exclusions retain the original source row, reason and mapping history. Included children need an included local parent or an explicit existing provider parent.\n\n| Field family | Conversion |\n| --- | --- |\n| Resource Public | `yes` → public; `no` → restricted; blank → private |\n| Resource Featured | Yes/no to the provider's Boolean representation |\n| Media Public / 360 Video | Yes/no to the provider's Boolean representation |\n| Transcript/index Public | The provider's `is_public` value |\n| Supplemental Public | The provider's yes/no `access` value |\n| Sequence # | Positive integer in the native CSV; ordered dispatch within the relevant parent |\n| Metadata | `|` separates values; `;;` separates vocabulary and value where present |\n| Thumbnail | Select a local path or a URL; retain the chosen source and its distinct delivery action |\n\nResource metadata uses the provider's resource labels. Media metadata uses lowercase underscore field names. Additional mapped resource/media columns remain explicit custom metadata. Receiving collections supply their own available fields, vocabularies and geolocation semantics.\n\nThe maintained templates contain source defects that require deliberate mapping: transcript/index `Tile` headers where the importer reads `Title`, a repeated media key, and unquoted commas that widen a resource row. The full importer also reads Alt Date and Call Sign fields absent from its resource template. The workbench retains these inputs and requires an explicit correction or exclusion.\n\nThe REST schema has no transcript/index attachment sequence request parameter. The client dispatches their selected rows in Sequence # order and retains the numeric field in the native CSV and saved review. It does not invent a REST sort field or report unobserved provider-side ordering. Media `sort_order` follows the maintained importer.\n\n## Configuration and requests\n\nRequests use the selected organization HTTPS origin plus `/api/v1/`. The API token is read from the named process environment variable; its value is not saved. The maintained importer uses Bearer authorization, and configuration also permits the provider's raw authorization form.\n\nThe captured schema requires an `organization-id` header on every API endpoint. Both `organizationId` and `collectionId` must therefore be positive integer IDs. The normal client does not dispatch with a missing organization. Loopback HTTP is available only through the explicit local receiving configuration.\n\n~~~json\n{\n  \"schema\": \"stellar-forge.aviary-client.v1\",\n  \"baseUrl\": \"https://yourorganization.aviaryplatform.com\",\n  \"organizationId\": \"5\",\n  \"collectionId\": \"43\",\n  \"tokenEnv\": \"AVIARY_TOKEN\",\n  \"authorizationScheme\": \"Bearer\",\n  \"partSize\": 104857600,\n  \"multipartThreshold\": 104857600,\n  \"timeoutSeconds\": 120\n}\n~~~\n\n| Operation | Provider route and original payload | Retained result |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Create resource | POST resources; JSON collection_id, title, access, metadata and selected resource fields | Response `data.update.id` or record `data.id` |\n| Create linked/embed media | POST media_files; original parent, link/embed, metadata and media_file object | Original media ID |\n| Create local media | POST media_files; parent, filename, display/access/order query and multipart media_file field containing presigned | Media ID and original storage upload description |\n| Create staged media | POST media_files with original media_staging_id and parent parameters | Media ID |\n| Upload file bytes | PUT each original storage URL with its exact range and Content-Length | Media/upload/part identity, byte count, SHA256 and returned ETag |\n| Complete local media | GET media_files/{id}/complete; multipart adds original upload_id and parts_count | Separate mutation action and its endpoint acknowledgement |\n| Save media metadata | PUT media_files/{id}; original JSON metadata and empty media_file object | Original media ID and separate metadata action |\n| Set local thumbnail | PUT media_files/{id}/thumbnail; multipart binary field `thumbnail_image` | Original media ID, selected source bytes/hash and provider acknowledgement |\n| Add transcript/index | POST transcripts or indexes; multipart associated_file and original media parent fields | Actual attachment ID |\n| Add supplemental file | POST supplemental_files; multipart associated_file and original resource parent fields | Actual supplemental ID |\n| Read target membership | GET collections/{collection_id}/resources with page_number and page_size | Exact collection pages and original resource membership |\n| Read transcript exports | GET resources/{id}, transcripts/{id}, associated media model, and each declared export file | Original resource/media/transcript/format and exact file bytes |\n\nSupplemental files belong to resources. Their creation occurs once per supplemental row outside the media loop. A retained resource creation remains separate from the state of its media and attachments.\n\nThe client treats HTTP 200 with explicit `success: false`, including the transcript/index/supplemental response forms, as a provider rejection. Nested error objects retain their actual response and meaning. HTTP authentication, permission, rate-limit, conflict and server responses remain distinct.\n\n## Parent and collection binding\n\nExisting resource IDs are read from their original endpoint before child work. The resource GET is documented with both `data.id` and `data.resource_id` examples; the client accepts either and rejects a response containing different values for the two.\n\nA returned collection_id must equal the selected collection. A usable provider direct_url must identify the same resource and collection. When the resource model exposes neither, the client follows the documented collection-scoped route:\n\n~~~text\nGET collections/{collection_id}/resources?page_number=1&page_size=100\nGET collections/{collection_id}/resources?page_number=2&page_size=100\n~~~\n\nIts response is `{data: [...], total_entries: N}`. Pages are followed until the selected resource is found or the full reported set is exhausted. Repeated IDs, conflicting ID aliases, changing totals, premature empty pages and counts exceeding the total are explicit receiving errors. A short nonterminal page does not stop the walk.\n\nExisting media IDs are read from their original endpoint. Their `collection_resource_id` must match the selected original resource, which is itself checked against the collection. If the resource exposes its documented `media_file_id` array, that array must contain the media ID. Fresh media readback refreshes the resource model so a newly created child is not compared with a cached pre-creation list.\n\nOriginal-record reconciliation uses the same parent checks. It also compares requested title, filename, display name and custom identifier where those fields were part of the retained creation. The operator's discovery note is stored with the actual readback.\n\nTranscript export validates each transcript's documented `resource_file_id` through its media and resource. Selecting an arbitrary transcript ID from another collection cannot silently add it to the current handoff.\n\n## Local media, thumbnails and source bytes\n\nThe maintained importer uses one presigned PUT for smaller media and multipart upload for larger files. The default threshold and part size are 100 MiB. Configured part sizes range from 5 MiB to 5 GiB; the client preserves its 25,000,000,000-byte media ceiling. A multipart response supplies its original upload_id, part_size, parts_count and exactly one URL per contiguous part number. The final part contains the actual remaining bytes.\n\nThe client verifies the whole file length and SHA256 against the saved source, holds the source descriptor and reads exact ranges from that descriptor. Identity checks before and after reading bind transmitted bytes to the reviewed plan even if a pathname is replaced during a long migration. Attachments and local thumbnails use the same source mechanism. Empty selected upload files are rejected by the mapping review.\n\nAutomatic storage retries repeat the same original part and range. The Aviary token and organization header are never supplied to the separate storage origin. Completion retains the original media/upload identity and stays separate from metadata and attachments.\n\nA local thumbnail is uploaded only after the original media record exists. Its action key is `media:<Media User Key>:thumbnail`; the request contains the original file descriptor, logical source path, byte count and SHA256. The documented success body is an acknowledgement array such as `{\"data\":[\"The media file thumbnail updated successfully.\"]}`.\n\nFor a URL thumbnail, the maintained full importer supplies `thumbnail_path` in the media creation request. The client preserves that behavior and records `CREATE_PARAMETER_ACCEPTED` after the creation response. This parameter is supported by the maintained importer source, while the separately documented thumbnail endpoint handles local image bytes.\n\nSelecting both a local thumbnail and a URL is an explicit validation error before plan creation or provider dispatch. Both original cells remain in the review so the operator can choose one. Neither source silently takes precedence.\n\n## Recovery of an original action\n\nEvery action stores its immutable request before dispatch. Confirmation retains its response and provider ID. Interruption preserves the existing operation, original IDs, request hash and any accepted upload parts.\n\n| Original state | Receiving behavior |\n| --- | --- |\n| CONFIRMED / ADOPTED | Reuse the retained action and provider ID |\n| Unknown creation outcome | Read and explicitly adopt the selected original provider ID with a discovery note |\n| Unfinished storage part | Retry only its original upload identity and exact byte range |\n| Expired/redacted storage URLs | Supply current URLs for the original upload through `refresh_upload` |\n| Unknown completion outcome | Perform original-media and original-file reads; keep the completion mutation unchanged |\n| Unknown metadata update | Compare the original requested fields against the current original media record |\n| Unknown local thumbnail update | Compare the current original thumbnail bytes with the selected source |\n| Provider Retry-After | Retain its deadline and delay subsequent readback or dispatch |\n\nThe only automatic write retries are original storage parts. Media metadata and thumbnail PUTs retain uncertainty after a lost response instead of repeating a potentially significant update. Although completion uses GET, the endpoint changes provider state and is treated as a mutation.\n\nThe resource update documentation explicitly appends repeatable metadata and offers `[TRUNCATE]` to clear fields. The media update documentation does not provide a replacement/idempotency guarantee. The application therefore confirms interrupted media metadata through an original-record read, comparing every requested value/vocabulary pair with its multiplicity. Additional unrelated values may remain. HTML or vocabulary normalization that prevents an exact comparison leaves the action unresolved for operator review.\n\n### Lost media creation and upload URLs\n\nUse the retained action's original provider ID:\n\n~~~python\nimport aviary_client as client\n\nclient.reconcile(\n    workspace, operation_id, \"media:1001:create\", original_media_id,\n    \"Original media record located in the receiving collection.\"\n)\nclient.refresh_upload(workspace, operation_id, \"1001\", original_upload_record)\nclient.run(workspace, operation_id)\n~~~\n\nThe media GET model is not documented to return multipart_upload or presigned_url. Upload URL recovery is a separate explicit step using the receiving provider's original upload record.\n\nIf no upload identity was received before the creation response was lost, that first supplied record must match the original media ID, selected upload mode, retained source length and requested part size. Later records must preserve the already observed upload ID, part layout and every dispatched part binding. The original creation request and operator note remain unchanged.\n\nA completed upload bypasses expired or removed upload URLs when the workspace reopens. An unfinished part still requires a usable URL for the original upload.\n\n### Lost completion response\n\nThe completion endpoint's example identifies the original media and a Boolean `processing` value, although its published JSON example has a syntax error. The client accepts a valid matching record, including a one-record data array, with an actual Boolean. An ambiguous or malformed response remains uncertain.\n\nOn an uncertain original completion, `run` reconstructs completion parameters from confirmed immutable part receipts and preserves the original parameter representation. It does not create a second upload, repeat accepted parts or call the mutating completion endpoint again.\n\nPositive readback requires all of these observed facts:\n\n1. The original media ID and resource/collection binding still match.\n2. The documented `media_info_metadata` includes one General record whose FileSize matches the retained source.\n3. The documented `media_download_url` returns exactly the original byte count and SHA256.\n4. Every original upload part remains confirmed and covers the whole original file contiguously.\n\nThe download is streamed and hashed without storing another media copy. Redirects retain their origin boundaries; credentials are supplied only to the original API origin. The resulting action becomes ADOPTED with `ORIGINAL_UPLOADED_BYTES_AVAILABLE`, its original request hash, file-analysis evidence and exact readback digest.\n\nThis is an inference from the observed original file and its provider analysis. It does not reconstruct the lost completion response. The media GET schema exposes no processing-status field, so that processing value remains unknown in the readback receipt. Missing analysis, an unavailable file, a transcode with different bytes, or inconsistent identity leaves the original completion uncertain. A later `run` performs those reads again after any recorded retry deadline.\n\n### Lost metadata or thumbnail response\n\nMetadata recovery automatically reads the same media ID and requires all original requested fields. A matching read becomes ADOPTED with `REQUESTED_MEDIA_METADATA_PRESENT`; the original PUT request stays byte-identical.\n\nThumbnail recovery reads the same original media and its documented thumbnail_url, then hashes the returned image against the selected local source. Exact matches become ADOPTED with `ORIGINAL_THUMBNAIL_BYTES_AVAILABLE`. If the provider transforms the thumbnail bytes, the original action remains unresolved for an explicit provider review.\n\nThese readbacks run automatically when `run` encounters an uncertain original action. The explicit `reconcile` function also accepts the same completion, metadata and thumbnail action keys, but the supplied ID must equal the ID already present in that immutable request. Repeating reconciliation of an already retained terminal action with the same ID reuses the result.\n\n## Result meaning and portable handoff\n\nA run's COMPLETE state covers confirmed or positively adopted record creation, requested metadata, source-file transfers and attachments. Its `mediaDelivery` entries distinguish original completion evidence, nullable `providerReportedProcessing`, and the selected thumbnail outcome. Aviary's later encoding and player availability remain provider lifecycle facts; they are reported only when the retained API result exposes them.\n\nThe transcript exporter reads `data.transcripts_id` from a bound resource and each transcript's `data.export` format map. A format supplies file_name and file. Exact bytes, response length and SHA256 are retained. Any explicit additional-page marker remains an incomplete result. Already retained downloads are reused only after their file identity matches.\n\nThe saved operation pins the workspace UUID, source manifest, mapping revision/hash, target configuration and operation ID. The full handoff includes application source, all original source files, SQLite state, mapping revisions, operations, selected native package, current review and retained transcript exports. A draft mapping can be exported alongside the latest usable native-package revision and its explicit availability status.\n\nProvider response/event copies remove temporary storage and signed download capability URLs. Original immutable action requests preserve their identity. The receiving operator supplies its own selected token environment. ZIP receiving verifies the complete member list, every file hash, safe paths, original workspace UUID and source manifest before publishing the received workspace.\n\nThe public USGS example preserves actual publisher media, transcript text, credit and rights provenance. The separate complete local API/storage receiving journey exercises the maintained application and its HTTP bytes, original IDs, multipart ranges, thumbnail transfer, interruption recovery and portable reopen. An institution's live migration uses its selected organization, collection and normal Aviary service.\n"
    },

      "content": "# Aviary migration workspace — operator guide\n\nThis workspace takes an original audiovisual collection, records an explicit mapping into Aviary’s five import tables, and retains the source files, review revisions, import progress, provider IDs and receiving evidence together. The same reviewed collection can produce an Aviary bulk-import ZIP or drive the API workflow for an entered organization and collection.\n\nStart with the public USGS example below. For an institutional collection, substitute its original files and reviewed mappings, then choose the receiving collection and its visibility settings. The local preview and native CSV package can be inspected before any API operation.\n\n## What is included\n\nThe application consists of aviary.py, aviary_client.py, server.py, index.html, app.js, cli.mjs, this guide and PROVIDER_CONTRACT.md. The complete native handoff also includes managed.py and [the Applications guide](APPLICATIONS.md). The installed aviary command and the Aviary collection migration entry in Applications open that same workspace with its selected Python. Python 3.11 or later runs the application. The local command line and browser use the same retained workspace. In the surrounding Node project, `node research/aviary/cli.mjs` forwards the same arguments to Python and preserves normal process signals. producer reports that precise missing evidence instead of inventing acceptance
or replaying the completed mapping/provider workflow.

## Resume an actually saved checkpoint

This option accepts an already-authorized local copy of a checkpoint created by
this producer. It makes no remote file transfer or sharing change.

    python3 -B complete_aviary_delivery.py \
      --input aviary-delivery-input.json \
      --restore-checkpoint original-checkpoint-selection.json

The selection JSON contains exactly:

    {
      "path": "/actual/already-authorized/local/checkpoint.zip",
      "bytes": 123,
      "sha256": "ACTUAL_FULL_SHA256",
      "file_id": "ACTUAL_RETURNED_FILE_ID",
      "library_file_id": "ACTUAL_RETURNED_LIBRARY_FILE_ID",
      "saveReceipt": {
        "...": "THE_COMPLETE_ORIGINAL_EMITTED_SAVE_RECEIPT"
      }
    }

The complete saveReceipt is the providerReceipt field of the checkpoint result,
also emitted as saveReceipt with RECEIVING_CHECKPOINT_SAVED. Keep its complete
original fields. Placeholder values are not accepted evidence.

The restore holds one original archive descriptor, validates every unique
regular member against DELIVERY_MEMBERS.json before publishing any file, binds
the manifest to this original root/source/workspace/operation, and reuses exact
existing prefix files. It also restores the original checkpoint's save receipt
at its original source pathname. Reopening that checkpoint does not upload it
again. A completed browser checkpoint is reused even after later visual
inspection advances the workspace.

The checkpoint requires the two original accepted archives to remain available
at their original authorized locations. It contains their exact identities and
restoration manifests rather than duplicating their completed receiving.

On a caught failure, the producer first verifies that its recorded commands
have drained. It retains the exact failure and attempts one
INTERRUPTED_RECEIVING checkpoint using the same canonical save route. If a
command remains unresolved or the save fails, the output explicitly reports
that the checkpoint was not saved. It does not claim success or redispatch an
unknown command.

      }

    if(!live.length)break;
  }

async function spawnChild(command,argv,label,{stdin=false,cwd=APP,timeoutMs=90000}={}){

async function finishChild(entry,{stop=false,normal=false}={}){

  }

  catch(error){
    for(const signal of ['SIGTERM','SIGKILL']){
      if(entry.closed)break;try{process.kill(-entry.child.pid,signal);}catch(e){if(e.code!=='ESRCH')throw e;}
      await deadline(entry.closePromise,5000,'Child '+entry.label+' '+signal).catch(()=>{});

function jobIdentity(job){
  expect(job&&typeof job.id==='string'&&typeof job.kind==='string'&&typeof job.created==='string'&&job.arguments&&typeof job.arguments==='object','Original queued job identity is incomplete');
  return {id:job.id,kind:job.kind,arguments:job.arguments,created:job.created};

function jobMatches(job,intent){
  if(job.kind!==intent.kind||intent.beforeJobIds.includes(job.id))return false;
  if(!job.arguments||typeof job.arguments.output!=='string')return false;
  if(intent.kind==='native-package'&&job.arguments.revision!=null&&Number(job.arguments.revision)!==intent.selection.revision)return false;
  const expectedDirectory=path.join(path.dirname(WORKSPACE),path.basename(WORKSPACE)+'-deliveries');
  if(path.resolve(path.dirname(job.arguments.output))!==expectedDirectory)return false;
  const prefix=intent.kind==='native-package'?'Aviary_Native_Package_':'Aviary_Complete_Workspace_';
  return path.basename(job.arguments.output).startsWith(prefix)&&job.arguments.output.endsWith('.zip');
}
async function retainedQueueResponse(name,intent,capturedRequest){

    const filename=path.join(ROOT,'runs',run,name+'.response.json');
    const response=await optionalJson(filename);
    if(!response)continue;
    expect(response.schema===SCHEMA&&response.route===intent.route&&isDeepStrictEqual(response.request,capturedRequest.body),'Original queued HTTP capture changed');
    const job=response.response?.value?.job;
    if(job&&jobMatches(job,intent))matches.push(jobIdentity(job));
  }
  const unique=new Map(matches.map(value=>[value.id,value]));
  expect(unique.size<=1,'More than one original accepted job is bound to this request');
  return [...unique.values()][0]||null;
}
async function queueOutput(name,{kind,route,selection,trigger}){

      beforeJobIds:jobs.jobs.map(job=>job.id).sort(),createdAt:new Date().toISOString()};

  const bindingPath=path.join(directory,'original-job.json'),requestPath=path.join(directory,'request.json');

    if(fromResponse){
      job=jobs.jobs.find(value=>value.id===fromResponse.id);

      binding=fromResponse;
    }else if(capturedRequest){

      expect(candidates.length<=1,'Queued response is uncertain and more than one persisted job could match; preserve all original jobs');
      if(candidates.length===1){job=candidates[0];binding=jobIdentity(job);}
    }

  }
  if(!binding){
    await ensureCurrent(selection.revision,selection.document);
    await page.locator('[data-tab=delivery]').click();
    const exchange=await uiExchange(route,trigger,async body=>{
      expect(body&&typeof body==='object'&&!Array.isArray(body),'Original queued request body is absent');
      if(kind==='native-package'&&body.revision!=null)expect(Number(body.revision)===selection.revision,'Original package request revision differs');

    },{label:name});

    jobs=await get('/api/jobs');job=jobs.jobs.find(value=>value.id===binding.id);
    expect(job&&isDeepStrictEqual(jobIdentity(job),binding),'Original persisted job changed or disappeared');
    if(['COMPLETED','FAILED','INTERRUPTED'].includes(job.state))break;
    expect(['QUEUED','RUNNING'].includes(job.state),'Original queued state is unsupported');
    if(Date.now()>=until)throw new Error('Original job '+job.id+' is still '+job.state+'; retain its output and reconcile after the owned server drains');
    await sleep(100);
  }
  const payload={job:binding,selection:intent.selection,applicationSource:sourcePin.files};
  let observed=await support('verify-job',payload,name+'-verify');
  if(observed.state==='MISSING'&&job.state==='INTERRUPTED'){
    await closeServer();
    observed=await support('resume-job',payload,name+'-resume-original');
    await openServer(APP,WORKSPACE);await openPage();
  }
  expect(observed.state==='VERIFIED','Original queued output is incomplete; no replacement job was created: '+JSON.stringify({job:binding.id,state:job.state,output:binding.arguments.output}));
  expect(observed.archive.output===binding.arguments.output,'Verified original output path differs');
  if(completed){
    expect(completed.job.id===binding.id&&completed.archive.sha256===observed.archive.sha256&&completed.archive.bytes===observed.archive.bytes,'Completed original queue output changed');
    await verifyFile(completed.archive.file);return completed;
  }
  completed=await completeStep(name,{job:binding,observedOriginalJobState:observed.job.state,
    archive:observed.archive,verification:observed,originalJobRecordPreserved:true});
  return completed;
}
async function publishCaptured(capture){

  expect(capture.pendingPath&&await exists(capture.pendingPath),'Retained capture bytes are unavailable; preserve its original descriptor');
  await verifyFile({...capture.file,path:capture.pendingPath});
  try{await link(capture.pendingPath,filename);}catch(error){if(error.code!=='EEXIST')throw error;await verifyFile(capture.file);}
  await syncDirectory(path.dirname(filename));await verifyFile(capture.file);
  await unlink(capture.pendingPath).catch(error=>{if(error.code!=='ENOENT')throw error;});
  return capture.file;
}

    if(child.stdin)child.stdin.on('error',()=>{});
    const observer=await processObserver();
    // ChildProcess.pid is relative to this process namespace; it is not a /proc host directory.
    entry.record=child.pid&&observer.hostPid===process.pid?await processRecord(child.pid):null;
    await publish(prefix+'.process.json',{pid:child.pid||null,record:entry.record,observer,identityMethod:'OWNED_CHILDPROCESS',owner:ownerMarker,launch:launch});
    return entry;
  }catch(error){
    if(child?.pid){try{process.kill(-child.pid,'SIGKILL');}catch{}}
    throw error;
  }finally{await stdout.close();if(stderr)await stderr.close();}
}
async function finishChild(entry,{stop=false,normal=false}={}){
  if(!entry)return null;
  if(stop&&!entry.closed){
    try{process.kill(-entry.child.pid,'SIGINT');}catch(error){if(error.code!=='ESRCH')throw error;}
  }
  let ended;
  try{ended=await deadline(entry.closePromise,stop?15000:entry.launch.timeoutMs,'Child '+entry.label);}
  catch(error){
    for(const signal of ['SIGTERM','SIGKILL']){
      if(entry.closed)break;try{process.kill(-entry.child.pid,signal);}catch(e){if(e.code!=='ESRCH')throw e;}
      await deadline(entry.closePromise,5000,'Child '+entry.label+' '+signal).catch(()=>{});
    }
    if(!entry.closed)throw error;
    ended=entry.exit;
    if(!stop)throw new Error('Child exceeded its receiving deadline: '+entry.label);
  }
  children.delete(entry);
  const stdout=await fileRecord(entry.launch.stdout),stderr=await fileRecord(entry.launch.stderr);
  const record={label:entry.label,pid:entry.child.pid||null,exit:ended,stdout,stderr,stdioClosed:true,at:new Date().toISOString()};
  await publish(path.join(RUN,entry.label+'.drain.json'),record);drains.push(record);
  if(normal)expect(ended.code===0&&!ended.spawnError,'Original child failed: '+entry.label+' '+JSON.stringify(ended));
  return record;
}
async function waitFirstJson(entry,label){
  const until=Date.now()+30000;
  while(Date.now()<until){
    const file=await readFile(entry.launch.stdout);
    expect(file.length<1024*1024,'Startup output is unexpectedly large: '+label);
    const text=file.toString('utf8'),end=text.indexOf('\n');
    if(end>=0)return JSON.parse(text.slice(0,end));
    if(entry.closed)throw new Error(label+' exited before readiness: '+(await readFile(entry.launch.stderr,'utf8')));
    await sleep(50);
  }
  throw new Error(label+' startup timed out');
}

function deferred(){
  let resolve,reject;const promise=new Promise((yes,no)=>{resolve=yes;reject=no;});promise.catch(()=>{});return {promise,resolve,reject};
}
async function uiExchange(routePath,trigger,onRequest,{hold=null,label='ui-request'}={}){
  expect(lockChild&&!lockChild.closed,'Original receiving lock is no longer held');
  expect(page&&currentServer,'Original page is unavailable');
  const reached=deferred(),done=deferred(),gate=deferred();
  let seen=false,released=false,responseObject=null,routeError=null,typing=null;
  const release=()=>{if(!released){released=true;gate.resolve();}};
  const pattern='**'+routePath;
  const handler=async route=>{
    if(route.request().method()!=='POST'){await route.continue();return;}
    if(seen){const error=new Error('More than one original mutation was dispatched for '+label);routeError=error;reached.reject(error);done.reject(error);await route.abort('failed').catch(()=>{});return;}
    seen=true;
    try{
      const request=route.request(),body=JSON.parse(request.postData()||'null');
      expect(new URL(request.url()).origin===currentServer.origin,'Mutation origin changed');
      await onRequest(body);
      expect(lockChild&&!lockChild.closed,'Original receiving lock closed before dispatch');
      responseObject=await route.fetch({timeout:30000});
      const raw=await responseObject.body();expect(raw.length<=16*1024*1024,'Original mutation response exceeds receiving bounds');
      const value=JSON.parse(raw.toString('utf8'));
      const response={status:responseObject.status(),value,bytes:raw.length,sha256:hash(raw)};
      await publishBytes(path.join(RUN,label+'.response-body.json'),raw);
      await publish(path.join(RUN,label+'.response.json'),{schema:SCHEMA,route:routePath,request:body,response,observedAt:new Date().toISOString()});
      reached.resolve(response);
      if(hold)await deadline(gate.promise,45000,'Held original mapping response');
      await route.fulfill({response:responseObject});
      done.resolve(response);
    }catch(error){
      routeError=error;reached.reject(error);done.reject(error);
      await route.abort('failed').catch(()=>{});
    }finally{if(responseObject)await responseObject.dispose().catch(()=>{});}
  };
  const routeRecord={page,pattern,handler,release,done:done.promise};routes.add(routeRecord);
  await page.route(pattern,handler);
  try{
    await deadline(Promise.resolve().then(trigger),30000,'Original UI trigger '+label);
    const response=await deadline(reached.promise,40000,'Original UI response '+label);
    expect(response.status>=200&&response.status<300,'Original UI request failed '+routePath+': '+JSON.stringify(response));
    if(hold){
      await page.locator('#mappingNote').fill(hold.laterNote);
      const beforeRelease=await page.locator('#mappingNote').inputValue();
      release();await deadline(done.promise,15000,'Original response release '+label);
      await page.waitForFunction(()=>!document.getElementById('saveMapping').disabled&&document.getElementById('mappingDirty').textContent.startsWith('Unsaved'));
      typing={
        observedAt:new Date().toISOString(),laterNote:hold.laterNote,inputBeforeRelease:beforeRelease,
        inputAfterRelease:await page.locator('#mappingNote').inputValue(),
        dirtyText:await page.locator('#mappingDirty').innerText(),saveEnabled:await page.locator('#saveMapping').isEnabled(),
        response:{status:response.status,bytes:response.bytes,sha256:response.sha256}
      };
      expect(typing.inputBeforeRelease===hold.laterNote&&typing.inputAfterRelease===hold.laterNote&&typing.saveEnabled&&typing.dirtyText.startsWith('Unsaved'),'Later operator typing was lost after the original save response');
    }else await deadline(done.promise,15000,'Original UI request completion '+label);
    if(routeError)throw routeError;
    return {response,typing};
  }finally{
    release();
    if(seen)await deadline(done.promise.catch(()=>{}),10000,'Route handler release '+label).catch(error=>cleanupErrors.push(briefError(error)));
    await page.unroute(pattern,handler);routes.delete(routeRecord);
  }
}
async function mappingStep(name,{before,route='/api/mapping',context:stepContext={},expectedDocument=null,prepare,trigger,hold=null}){

  const intentPath=path.join(directory,'intent.json');

  };

    expect(evidence?.committed&&isDeepStrictEqual(complete.mapping,evidence.mapping),'Completed mapping phase lost its original committed review: '+name);
    if(complete.typingFence)await verifyFile(complete.typingFence);

      }else expect(route==='/api/assign-keys'&&!Object.hasOwn(body,'document'),'Unexpected assignment request');
      const record={schema:SCHEMA,inputSha256:identity.inputSha256,route,body};

        expect(existing.requestSha256===hash(encoded(captured))&&existing.typing.laterNote===hold.laterNote,'Original typing observation binding differs');
      }else await publish(filename,{schema:SCHEMA,inputSha256:identity.inputSha256,requestSha256:hash(encoded(captured)),typing:exchange.typing});

    expect(fence.inputSha256===identity.inputSha256&&fence.requestSha256===hash(encoded(captured))&&fence.typing.inputAfterRelease===fence.typing.laterNote&&fence.typing.saveEnabled,'Typing observation no longer binds the committed save');

function jobIdentity(job){
  expect(job&&typeof job.id==='string'&&typeof job.kind==='string'&&typeof job.created==='string'&&job.arguments&&typeof job.arguments==='object','Original queued job identity is incomplete');
  return {id:job.id,kind:job.kind,arguments:job.arguments,created:job.created};
}
function jobMatches(job,intent){
  if(job.kind!==intent.kind||intent.beforeJobIds.includes(job.id))return false;
  if(!job.arguments||typeof job.arguments.output!=='string')return false;
  if(intent.kind==='native-package'&&job.arguments.revision!=null&&Number(job.arguments.revision)!==intent.selection.revision)return false;
  const expectedDirectory=path.join(path.dirname(WORKSPACE),path.basename(WORKSPACE)+'-deliveries');
  if(path.resolve(path.dirname(job.arguments.output))!==expectedDirectory)return false;
  const prefix=intent.kind==='native-package'?'Aviary_Native_Package_':'Aviary_Complete_Workspace_';
  return path.basename(job.arguments.output).startsWith(prefix)&&job.arguments.output.endsWith('.zip');
}
async function retainedQueueResponse(name,intent,capturedRequest){
  if(!capturedRequest)return null;
  const matches=[];
  for(const run of await readdir(path.join(ROOT,'runs'))){
    const filename=path.join(ROOT,'runs',run,name+'.response.json');
    const response=await optionalJson(filename);
    if(!response)continue;
    expect(response.schema===SCHEMA&&response.route===intent.route&&isDeepStrictEqual(response.request,capturedRequest.body),'Original queued HTTP capture changed');
    const job=response.response?.value?.job;
    if(job&&jobMatches(job,intent))matches.push(jobIdentity(job));
  }
  const unique=new Map(matches.map(value=>[value.id,value]));
  expect(unique.size<=1,'More than one original accepted job is bound to this request');
  return [...unique.values()][0]||null;
}

    const jobs=await get('/api/jobs');
    intent={schema:SCHEMA,inputSha256:identity.inputSha256,step:name,kind,route,
      selection:{workspaceId:selection.workspaceId,revision:selection.revision,mappingSha256:selection.mappingSha256,sourceManifestSha256:selection.sourceManifestSha256},
      beforeJobIds:jobs.jobs.map(job=>job.id).sort(),createdAt:new Date().toISOString()};
